subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Land Rover engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the AJ133 across its 2 model applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The AJ133 is fitted across Defender, Range Rover Velar — we see it regularly across the full application range.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Bearings, timing chain components, gaskets, and twin-scroll turbocharger components as standard. We also inspect and measure the cylinder head, crankshaft, and other critical components.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: No widely-reported failure pattern is confirmed for the AJ133 across its applications. We don't treat this engine as having one universal failure mode; diagnosis is required to establish whether an engine needs repair, rebuild, or replacement.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page — they'll be added once a documented set of completed AJ133 rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.

typical.title: LAND ROVER AJ133 REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: A full AJ133 rebuild involves stripping the engine down, inspecting the crankshaft, cylinder head and timing components, and replacing worn bearings, gaskets and seals with updated OEM-specification parts (V8 (90° angle), 5.0L (5,000 cc), Petrol, Petrol Supercharged).

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Timing chain, bearings, gaskets, twin-scroll turbocharger inspection/refurbishment, calibration of fuel injection system
